1: Chapter 1: The Visitor on a Rainy Night

It had rained in Qingshi for three days straight. Lin Xiaoyu closed the door of the pharmacy and lit the last lamp. She was twenty-two, and since her father's death she had kept the little shop going on her own.
"Is anyone there?" a man's voice called from outside.

Lin Xiaoyu hesitated for a moment, then opened the door. A young man stood in the doorway, soaked through, his left hand clutching his right arm with blood seeping between his fingers. He said his name was Chen Ziming and that he had come from the provincial capital.
"I need to get this bandaged," Chen Ziming said in a low voice. "I can pay. Is a hundred and twenty yuan enough?"

She didn't take his money, just had him sit down by the counter and turned to get gauze and medicinal wine. The wound wasn't deep, but it was long, as if slashed by a knife. As she cleaned it, she asked him how he had been hurt.

Chen Ziming was silent for a long time before he said, "I ran into some men on the road. They wanted a letter I was carrying." He took an oil-paper parcel from inside his clothes and put it on the table. "This letter has to be delivered to Baiyun before May 18."

Lin Xiaoyu glanced out the window. Baiyun was up in the mountains, forty li from Qingshi, and the mountain road was hardest to travel when it rained. She remembered what her father always used to say: if you save someone, see it through to the end.
"I'll take you up the mountain first thing tomorrow morning," she said. "You can sleep in the back room tonight."
2: Before dawn, Lin Xiaoyu woke Chen Ziming. She put on her bamboo basket, which held dry rations, herbal medicine, and an old umbrella. Chen Ziming's arm was a little better, but his face was still pale.
Halfway up the mountain, they ran into Zhou Dashan, an old woodcutter. Zhou Dashan knew Lin Xiaoyu and asked her with a smile where she was headed so early.
"To deliver medicine to Baiyun," Lin Xiaoyu answered. She didn't mention the letter.
Zhou Dashan glanced at Chen Ziming and lowered his voice. "Yesterday evening, three outsiders were at the entrance to town asking about an injured young man. Be careful."

Chen Ziming went even paler. Lin Xiaoyu thanked the old man and led Chen Ziming off the main road onto a small trail known only to herb gatherers. The trail was narrow and slippery, and she walked ahead, placing each step firmly.

By noon, the rain had finally stopped. The mist in the mountains slowly cleared, and in the distance the roof of Baiyun came into view. At the temple gate stood a nun named Zhao Qiuyue, the temple's guest prefect.
Zhao Qiuyue took the oil-paper package, looked at the red seal on it, and nodded. "Master has been waiting 2 years for this letter," she said. "You've gone to a lot of trouble."
On the way back, Chen Ziming said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled and said, "Then next time you come to Qingshi, help me fix the roof of the medicine shop."
